title: An isolated point of a scheme locally of finite type over a field has residue field finite over the field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be a morphism which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $y\in Y$ be a point such that the singleton $\{y\}$ is open in $Y$ ($y$ is an isolated point of $Y$). Then the residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field], made a field extension of $k$ by the homomorphism $k\to\kappa(y)$ induced by $g$ on residue fields (the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ at its unique point being $k$), is a finite extension: $\dim_k\kappa(y)<\infty$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00PJ (algebra-lemma-isolated-point, line 30106), (1) => (6) (via its proof: Spec of a finite type k-algebra is Jacobson, Lemmas 00G1 (algebra-lemma-finite-type-field-Jacobson) and 00G3 (algebra-lemma-jacobson), so an isolated prime is closed, hence maximal, and Theorem 00FV (algebra-theorem-nullstellensatz, line 6524) gives the residue field finite), applied to an affine open Spec B of Y containing y with B of finite type over k (Morphisms, Lemma 01T2 lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); this is the case S = Spec k of Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, line 3664), (2) => (4), with Lemma 01TG (morphisms-lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite, line 3652); compare the proof of Morphisms, Lemma 01TF (morphisms-lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type, line 3597)

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, write $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ correspond to $y$ under the canonical open immersion $\iota: \operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Since $g(Y)$ is the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, the pair of affine opens $U\subseteq Y$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}k$ satisfies the criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]; hence the structure map $k\to B$ is of finite type. The inverse image of the open singleton $\{y\}$ under $\iota$ is the singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}$, so $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), (1) => (2), applied to the affine chart U over Spec(k); the affine chart and its point are Schemes, Tag 01IJ and Lemma 01HH

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-prime-finite-type-algebra-residue-finite] to $k$, $B$, and $\mathfrak p$. It gives that $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ for the map $k\to B\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00PJ (algebra-lemma-isolated-point), implication (1) => (6), after restricting to the finite type affine chart

proof.text: The affine chart identifies the scheme residue field $\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}B}(\mathfrak p)$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification]. The open immersion $\iota$ identifies $\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}B}(\mathfrak p)$ with $\kappa(y)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] to the structure map $k\to B$ shows that these identifications carry the map from the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (which is $k$ at its unique point) to the map $k\to\kappa(y)$ induced by $g$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas 01HV and 01HY (stalks of affine schemes and maps into an affine scheme), together with the residue-field diagram after Lemma 01J9; the open-immersion residue-field assertion is Lemma 01HH

proof.text: Finite-dimensionality over $k$ is invariant under the $k$-linear field isomorphism in step 3. Therefore the residue field $\kappa(y)$, with the action of $k$ induced by $g$, is a finite extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension].
